summary:
Long-duration space missions under the Artemis and future Mars exploration programs present a major challenge: astronauts may experience medical emergencies in environments where communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable. Relying entirely on ground-based medical support is therefore not always practical.

AstroPulse Edge aims to address this challenge through a wearable health-monitoring system powered by the ESP32-S3 microcontroller. It continuously collects physiological data, including ECG, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, and body movement using dedicated sensors.

Instead of depending on cloud processing, the system uses lightweight Random Forest machine learning models directly on the device to identify potential cardiac abnormalities and changes in stress levels. The models are trained using the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia and WESAD datasets, with an approximate combined memory footprint of 796 KB.

A sensor-fusion mechanism combines information from multiple sources to identify potentially concerning health patterns. The collected data can also be transmitted over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) to a habitat monitoring dashboard, allowing crew members to view their health status and receive alerts without requiring an internet connection.
details:
1. Edge AI and Hardware Integration

The system is built around the ESP32-S3, which processes sensor readings locally. Machine learning models are converted into C-compatible decision trees and integrated directly into the firmware. This allows the device to perform real-time predictions without depending on external servers or continuous internet connectivity.

2. Autonomous Health Monitoring

AstroPulse Edge focuses on two important aspects of astronaut health: cardiac abnormalities and physiological stress. By continuously monitoring these parameters, the system aims to identify unusual patterns early and notify crew members when further attention may be required.

This approach is particularly relevant to the health risks identified in NASA's Human Research Roadmap, including cardiac rhythm problems, fatigue, and behavioral health challenges during space missions.

3. Dual Monitoring and Simulation Pipeline

The project includes both a physical wearable monitoring system and a software-based simulation environment. The simulator generates ECG waveforms, including P-Q-R-S-T complexes, allowing us to test the monitoring interface, classification models, and alert mechanisms even when physical sensors are unavailable.

Together, these components provide a practical foundation for developing autonomous health-monitoring technology for future space exploration.
